findings.location:
#s1-p1,

element, text 'Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk. Updates p...', line 20
findings.evidence: text color #999999 on background #ffffff, contrast ratio 2.85:1
findings.violation: Contrast ratio 2.85:1 is below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text.
findings.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio reaches at least 4.5:1.

findings.violation: The viewport meta tag sets user-scalable=no, disabling browser zoom entirely.
findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no so readers can zoom the page.

findings.violation: A fixed width of 960px forces horizontal scrolling once the viewport narrows to 320px, with no responsive override.
findings.fix: Cap the element's width with a relative max-width (a percentage or viewport unit), or add a media query that shrinks it below 320px.

findings.location: #nav, <nav> element, sole navigation mechanism on the page, line 11
findings.evidence: nav contains 2 links (Accessibility, Fares and passes); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail is present anywhere in the document
findings.violation: The page provides only one navigation mechanism, the primary nav, with no site search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail, and the page is not one step of a linear process that would exempt it.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent mechanism for locating this page, such as a site search form, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail.

findings.evidence: boundary color #9d9d9d against adjacent background #ffffff, contrast ratio 2.71:1
findings.violation: Component boundary contrast ratio 2.71:1 is below the 3:1 AA minimum.
findings.fix: Darken the border or outline color, or change the adjacent background, until the ratio reaches at least 3:1.

findings.violation: A fixed height combined with clipped overflow truncates this element's text once a reader applies wider line, paragraph, letter, or word spacing.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height so the element grows with its content, or replace the clipped overflow with visible or auto.

findings.evidence: heading text 'Accessibility improvements'; the section's body covers a schedule-kiosk notice, a mobile-app fare adjustment, and a photo of a platform operator, none of which concern accessibility
findings.violation: The heading's wording names an accessibility topic, but the section it introduces covers schedule and fare-adjustment content with no accessibility subject matter, misdescribing what actually follows it.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe the section's actual content, for example 'Schedule and fare updates', or move genuine accessibility content into this section.

findings.evidence: input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true" carries no aria-describedby; the sibling #s3-form-promo-error text 'Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.' is not referenced by any attribute on the input
findings.violation: The invalid promo field's error text exists in the markup but is not programmatically associated with the field, so a screen-reader user who tabs to the field does not hear the error description automatically.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input so its error text is announced when the field receives focus.

findings.violation: No label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title identifies what this control expects.
findings.fix: Add a <label for> pointing at this control's id, wrap the control in a <label>, or set aria-label.
